questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to italy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been more difficult being on exchange than expected. I have learned a lot, about myself, academic stuff  and other cultures, but there has also been some difficulties (mostly which is probably personal)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: pretty difficult

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: i tried to talk with other erasmus students i met to get to know the webpage of the university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: to be honest, I really had a lot of troubles finding out which courses were available, when to start, how the register.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: pretty easy for me - but i also started very early since I heard that it was difficult.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: nice to meet other people that the erasmus students or class mates. Different standards when it comes to cleaning, but over all a very very good experience

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was difficult

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: for me it was difficult to find out when the different courses took place, which ones I could take and so on. I started with some courses but switched th first couple of weeks.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: it was difficult to find someone at my own campus. I found out in the end, when i asked other students and teachers, but i felt pretty stupid and alone in the proces.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: im happy about the courses i enden up with, but only one of them were what I thought I should have when i arrived.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont stress - they take it very chill i italy. It is not like there is a very exact date as in Denmark. Everything will work out and they are very loose

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 5 because I found it very interest and high level. Im at my bachelor and took master courses (30 ETCS). For me it was very difficult. Much more difficult that expected. I had 7 exams in the period before I went home, so I will suggest to look at how th exams are for the courses you are taking

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: high level (exams were not so difficult, but the lessons were often difficult)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: only professors teaching. Not a lot of interaction

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced molecular biology, Molecular immunology and pharmacology, Synthetic biology, Molecular microbiology and genetics of microorganisms, Biomembranes

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Molecular microbiology and genetics of microorganisms (mostly because of my own interest -  but also the best teacher i think)

questions.answer: Take the train. To go on trips to lake of como, verona, torino, to the mountains in switzerland, napoli

questions.answer: pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with my roomies, their frinds and other erasmus students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
the thing about taking things so chill. 
Also the language!!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very open and friendly people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Say yes yes yes.
Go on trips
dont be stressed if you think school is difficult - it is okay (even when are at exchange)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: look at which campus you are at, if you are looking for housing before you go to milan

questions.answer: I learned so many things about my reaction on being on your own.
